products.name: InternLM (Shanghai AI Lab)
products.note: Chinese open-source LLM; academic research; cross-border data review advised

reading.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government-affiliated research institution in China operating InternLM, an open-source large language model positioned for academic research across Chinese universities and scientific applications.

The laboratory's stated focus spans model capability, embodied robotics, and AI safety frameworks, with recent emphasis on science-oriented systems that integrate language models, specialist agents, and physical automation. This portfolio suggests a research strategy prioritizing broad capability development rather than any single domain constraint. The 2026 announcement of AI-for-science results and a scientific discovery platform indicates the institution is testing large models as infrastructure for experimental workflows, from hypothesis through validation.

What matters for AI infrastructure is that Shanghai AI Laboratory operates within China's university and research ecosystem, not as a commercial infrastructure builder or power provider. The laboratory contributes to model capability and research methodology but does not control the compute, buildings, or power grids that determine how quickly those capabilities can scale. It represents the downstream user of infrastructure, not the constraint that binds it.

The data does not cover the laboratory's budget, its access to compute hardware, or the power requirements of its training and inference systems. Without those facts, the connection between its research ambitions and the infrastructure constraints that may or may not enable them remains unmeasured.

profile_text.body:
Shanghai AI Laboratory is a government laboratory, and its site describes it as not for profit. It says it recruits young researchers worldwide across artificial intelligence, large models, embodied intelligence, safe and trustworthy AI, AI for Science, basic platforms, the innovation chain and management support, with the stated aim of working toward AGI. Since 2022 it has run a joint doctoral training program with more than ten universities, among them Peking University, Tsinghua University, Fudan University, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tongji University, the University of Science and Technology of China and Zhejiang University.

Its tracked product is InternLM, listed under Chat and General LLMs and described as a Chinese open-source large language model used in academic research, with cross-border data review advised. The site also describes Mobius, an open-source architecture for long-horizon reasoning and scientific discovery, and Intern-Robotics, an embodied full-stack engine it says covers data, training and application. At the 2026 WAIC Science Frontier Forum it released the 书生·端砚 science discovery platform, which it says connects science models, specialist agents, experimental data and embodied automation equipment across a research process running from hypothesis to experimental verification, along with ten joint science intelligence results under the label 与书生共创, covering life sciences, materials science and deep space astronomy.

On safety, the laboratory describes a general and specialist fusion technical system in three layers, and an "AI-45 degree balance law" holding that safety and performance should follow roughly a 45 degree line over the long term, with short-term variation but no sustained departure in either direction. It says it is exploring a causal path toward trustworthy AGI through three stages it calls broad alignment, intervenability and reflection, and describes risk management spanning assessment, training, base, application and verification. It also states that its 2026 global campus recruitment is open and that it runs a "North Star" talent program.
